topic: DEFINITIVE root cause for the gen2/gen1 --version SIGSEGV residual, superseding the offset-level trace in artifacts/audit/madaros_gen2_argslist_field_offset_20260903.json (PR #2408). That document correctly traced the crash to ArgList.len being read from the wrong byte offset; this document identifies the exact source-level defect that produces the wrong offset.
summary: self-hosted/ir/lower.sio's field_idx_from_name(struct_name, field_name) -- the function that resolves a named field access like `lst.len` to a compile-time slot index -- has a real type-safety hole: when the requested struct type IS found in the layout table but the requested field is NOT found within THAT SPECIFIC entry, the function does not check whether a LATER entry in the table also carries the same struct_name (i.e. a second, possibly-complete registration of the same struct). Instead it falls straight through into a second loop that scans EVERY OTHER struct in the entire program by FIELD NAME ALONE, with no type checking, and returns the first field index it finds -- even though that field belongs to a completely unrelated struct type. For ArgList.len, this returned the field index of some OTHER struct's 'len' field (idx 48 in the compiled binary), producing the wrong byte offset traced in the companion document and ultimately the SIGSEGV.
exact_location: self-hosted/ir/lower.sio, fn field_idx_from_name (starts at line 12646). The defective control flow is the inner block starting 'Field not found in the named layout. Keep searching the rest of the table before falling back to the legacy hash path' (around line 12659) -- reached whenever field_name is not present among fields[0..field_count] of the FIRST struct_layouts entry whose type_name matches struct_name.

why_this_is_reachable_for_arglist_specif.acknowledged_precedent: self-hosted/ir/lower.sio's own comments (struct_layout_slot_count, ~line 7421) already document that a struct type CAN be registered more than once in struct_layouts -- 'a type registered twice — declaration pass plus import seeding — carries a DOUBLED field_count'. Three separate call sites register struct fields via lowerer_register_struct_fields_direct_mut (lines 2212, 3542, 3660, each REPLACING any existing entry for that type_name) and one via lowerer_register_struct_fields_mut (line 5339, called with idx=0 from the main per-module item-lowering pass over ItemStruct declarations, which APPENDS onto an existing entry rather than replacing).
why_this_is_reachable_for_arglist_specif.the_gap: field_idx_from_name's first loop takes the FIRST si where type_name matches struct_name and, if the field isn't in THAT entry, gives up on the named-type search entirely -- it never checks si+1, si+2, ... for another entry also named 'ArgList'. If ANY of the three _direct_mut call sites (2212 / 3542 / 3660) fires for ArgList at a point where its full field list (items, len) is not yet available -- e.g. an early/partial pass, or a distinct code path that legitimately only sees a subset of an imported struct's declared fields -- that registration would create (or leave) an ArgList entry lacking 'len'. A later, complete registration of ArgList elsewhere in the table would never be consulted, because the first (incomplete) match already short-circuited the search into the cross-struct fallback.
why_this_is_reachable_for_arglist_specif.not_yet_directly_observed: This session did not instrument field_idx_from_name itself to catch it deciding 48 for ArgList.len in situ (that would need another ~40-70 minute gen1/gen2 rebuild cycle to test on the full main.sio, since the isolated small-file repro in this session's earlier work did not reproduce the crash -- consistent with this bug needing enough OTHER structs registered in struct_layouts, each contributing candidate 'len' fields at various indices, plus a genuine ArgList double/partial-registration, for the collision to manifest at exactly this call site). The control-flow defect itself, however, is unambiguous from reading the function: ANY struct with a partially-registered layout entry earlier in table order than its complete one will silently borrow field indices from whatever other struct in the ~1552-item main.sio module happens to share a field name. 'len' is about as common a field name as exists in a compiler's data structures (buffers, arrays, string builders, token/arg lists), making it a near-certainty that SOME other struct registers 'len' before ArgList's complete registration is reached.

proposed_fix_shape.conservative: In field_idx_from_name's outer while loop, do not stop at the first si whose type_name matches struct_name if the field is absent from that entry -- continue the SAME loop (do not fall through to the cross-struct scan) to check for a later entry also named struct_name before giving up on the named-type search. Only fall through to the untyped cross-struct/hash fallback once every entry actually named struct_name has been checked and none contains the field.
proposed_fix_shape.safer_but_more_invasive: Fail closed (compile error) rather than silently borrowing an unrelated struct's field index, once it's established the named struct type IS registered but the specific field genuinely isn't found in any of its entries -- a field access on a known struct type that names a field the struct doesn't have should never have been accepted by the type checker in the first place, so reaching this point at IR-lowering time likely indicates the exact registration-completeness bug described above rather than a legitimately absent field.
proposed_fix_shape.not_attempted_this_session: No fix was written or tested. This is a documentation-only finding for the next session/PR to act on. Any fix needs the full gen1 rebuild -> gen2 self-compile -> gen2 --version verification cycle (~40-70 minutes per iteration) to confirm it resolves the crash without regressing the legacy cross-struct/hash fallback's own test coverage (self-hosted/native/suite.sio and friends reference str_eq/field-access behavior extensively).

relationship_to_companion_document: artifacts/audit/madaros_gen2_argslist_field_offset_20260903.json (this session, earlier) established WHERE the corruption is observable at runtime (ArgList.len read from stack offset 384/slot 48 instead of the real data at offset ~80) via gdb memory/register inspection, and flagged the Madaros-vs-lean_single struct layout model disagreement as a plausible but unconfirmed architectural cause. This document supersedes that architectural hypothesis with a concrete, read-and-verified source-level control-flow defect in field_idx_from_name that fully explains the observed offset without requiring the two-layout-model disagreement to be involved at all.
